dedupe_keys.name: realistic synthetic benchmark instances for multi objective district heating unit commitment berlin based

description: This data set holds 100 large-scale synthetic benchmark instances for lexicographic multi-objective optimisation of unit commitment in district heating systems, based on the Berlin network. It was published by Annika Buchholz, Stephanie Riedmüller, Passage Matthew and Janina Zittel with a companion arXiv paper that benchmarks the instances against the large Berlin network. Each instance gives the network topology, parameters and time series as a JSON graph, plus complete mixed-integer programming formulations in MPS format for each of three ranked objectives: minimise operating cost, then emissions, then maximise delivered heat. Instances vary the horizon (10 or 25 years at 4-hour steps), demand nodes, production sites, converter units, storage and fuel markets, in ten groups of ten, with 5 to 15 million variables each; an open generator is on the Zuse Institute Berlin GitLab. Coverage is one synthetic system modelled on Berlin. Files are ZIP archives on Zenodo (about 6.8 GB, published April 2026, updated June 2026) under CC-BY-4.0 at no cost. Caveats: the data are synthetic, not records of the real network, and the instances are very large for most solvers. Simulation uses are benchmarking solvers and optimisation methods for district heating dispatch and unit commitment. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
